title: Haskell Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Print a greeting
entries.summary: main is the starting action. putStrLn writes a line of text.
notes: Text uses double quotes; single quotes hold one character.

entries.name: Name a value
entries.summary: A name can stand for a value. Haskell names do not work like boxes that are updated later.
notes: Give the name one definition in this scope.

entries.name: Name a calculation
entries.summary: Functions take inputs written after their name. This function doubles a number.
notes: Function calls use spaces, not a required pair of call parentheses.

entries.name: Write a type guide
entries.summary: A type signature describes inputs and results. Int -> Int means a whole number in and out.

example.code:
twice :: Int -> Int
twice n = n * 2
main = print (twice 4)

notes: The definition must agree with its type signature.

entries.name: Choose with if
entries.summary: An if expression always has then and else parts because it must produce a value.

example.code:
message score = if score >= 5 then "Pass" else "Try again"
main = putStrLn (message 8)

notes: Both branches must produce the same kind of value.

entries.name: Read a short list
entries.summary: A list keeps values of one type in order. head reads the first item.
notes: head fails on an empty list; pattern matching can handle that case.

entries.name: Change every item
entries.summary: map applies a function to each list item and returns a new list.
notes: The original list is a value and is not changed in place.

entries.name: Keep matching items
entries.summary: filter keeps items that pass a true-or-false test.
notes: The test must return Bool, not a number.

entries.name: Handle list shapes
entries.summary: Pattern matching selects steps based on a value shape. [] is an empty list; x:_ has a first item.
notes: Cover the empty-list case before assuming an item exists.

entries.name: Repeat with a smaller job
entries.summary: A recursive function calls itself. This one stops at zero, then adds numbers on the way back.

example.code:
sumTo n
  | n <= 0 = 0
  | otherwise = n + sumTo (n - 1)
main = print (sumTo 3)

notes: A recursive function needs a case that stops.

entries.name: Show that a value may be absent
entries.summary: Maybe holds Nothing or Just a value. Pattern matching handles both safely.

example.code:
showScore Nothing = "No score"
showScore (Just n) = show n
main = putStrLn (showScore (Just 8))

notes: Handle both Nothing and Just cases.

entries.name: Build a list from a rule
entries.summary: A list comprehension chooses inputs, filters them and builds new results.
notes: Read the input and filter before working out the result.
